questions.problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve ${x}^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}xy, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[-1,1]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14099625/assets/736575dceb6969f8b45e4038f702ebc84347ab66a1a8e5ea5103840ddd61ba31.png)

Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}xy, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangle I does not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangles II and III cover the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
